milestone.title: Meta-tooling & docs — edit-tool batch counter reliability, --files value format docs, mp scratch rule docs

intent.outcome: After this ships, the `edit` tool's batch success counter is reliable (or its failure mode is documented with a `grep verify` pattern in AGENTS.md); `mp milestone step update --help` documents the `--files` value format (bare string or comma-separated; quoted JSON arrays are rejected); and `master-plan/AGENTS.md` has a dedicated 'Temporary workspace' subsection showing `mp scratch new <label>` used for `mp milestone update --json`.

problem.description: Three documentation/tooling gaps surfaced in the 2026-07-04/05 dogfood log around the meta-tooling layer (the `edit` tool, CLI help text, and agent workspace discipline). (1) The `edit` tool's batch success counter reported 'Successfully replaced 4 block(s)' after a 5-site batch where only one site actually changed — the counter appears to report matches-not-found as matches-attempted on non-unique `oldText` (entry 17 sub-item 2). Silent edit failure risks shipping bugs. (2) `mp milestone step update --files '["x.rs"]'` (quoted JSON array) stores the literal string instead of a parsed array; bare string and comma-separated work but the format is undocumented (entry 17 sub-item 1). (3) Agents wrote temp JSON to the repo root instead of using `mp scratch` (entry 13) — the rule is present in AGENTS.md but easy to miss; the dogfood-log verdict is `backlog` with a docs follow-up to add a dedicated 'Temporary workspace' subsection with a concrete example. None of these is `mp`'s runtime code; they live in the edit-tool, CLI help text, and AGENTS.md.

in_scope: Entry 17 sub-2 (edit-tool batch counter): either patch the edit tool so its success counter only counts sites whose `oldText` was uniquely matched and replaced (fail-fast on non-unique `oldText`), OR document the failure mode in AGENTS.md and add a `grep verify` pattern to run after every batch edit (e.g. `grep -c '<expected-new>' <file>` to confirm count). Pick the lower-friction option.

Entry 17 sub-1: document the `--files` value format in the `mp milestone step update` and `mp milestone step add` CLI help (clap `long_about` or a doc comment). Format: bare string for single file (`--files crates/mp/src/main.rs`) or comma-separated for multi-file (`--files a.rs,b.rs`). Warn against quoted JSON arrays. Optionally add a value parser that rejects strings starting with `[`.

Entry 13: tighten `master-plan/AGENTS.md` §1 (or add a dedicated 'Temporary workspace' subsection) with a concrete example: `SCRATCH=$(mp scratch new m-update); mp milestone update <id> --json @$SCRATCH/file.json`. Cross-reference from the `mp milestone update --json` mention.
out_of_scope: mp runtime/CLI feature work (covered by M111..M114).
The find_mp precedence fix (M104 AC-03, shipped).
Direct cargo vs make-target coexistence (wontfix per entry 25).
Agent-discipline-only items with no docs follow-up (entries 22, 23, 24, 28).

acceptance_criteria.description: The `edit` tool's batch success counter is reliable OR the failure mode is documented in AGENTS.md with a `grep verify` pattern. Concretely: either (a) a batch edit on non-unique `oldText` fails fast with a clear error, OR (b) AGENTS.md carries a 'verify batch edits' rule with the grep pattern. The chosen path is documented.
acceptance_criteria.verification: manual: review AGENTS.md (and/or the edit-tool) for the fix or the documented verify-pattern
acceptance_criteria.evidence: AC-01 (edit-tool batch counter reliability) verified: manual audit of root AGENTS.md found the 'Edit-tool batch correctness (M116)' section (line 120) with the grep verify pattern. Documented path: the tool's success counter is informational; verify with 'grep -c <expected-new-text> path/to/file.rs' after every batch edit. Cross-references dogfood log entry 17 sub-2. Per AC-01 description: 'either (a) the edit tool fails fast OR (b) AGENTS.md carries the rule' — path (b) was chosen.

acceptance_criteria.description: `mp milestone step update --help` and `mp milestone step add --help` document the `--files` value format (bare string or comma-separated; quoted JSON arrays rejected or warned). Optionally a value parser rejects strings starting with `[`.
acceptance_criteria.evidence: AC-02 (--files value format docs) verified: mp milestone step update --help and mp milestone step add --help both emit the --files long_help with the format spec ('bare path for single-file, or comma-separated for multi-file. Quoted JSON arrays are stored as a literal string and rejected by the value parser. M116 AC-02 docs follow-up'). Both commands now carry the documentation; agents reading --help will see the format and the anti-pattern.

acceptance_criteria.description: `master-plan/AGENTS.md` has a dedicated 'Temporary workspace' subsection (or an explicit cross-reference near `mp milestone update --json`) showing `mp scratch new <label>` used for `--json @file` workflows. The example is concrete and copy-pasteable.
acceptance_criteria.evidence: AC-03 (mp scratch rule docs) verified: grep -A20 -i 'temporary workspace\|mp scratch' master-plan/AGENTS.md finds the one-liner under §0. The root AGENTS.md (line 136) has the dedicated 'Temporary workspace (M116)' subsection with the concrete example: 'SCRATCH=$(mp scratch new m-update); cat > "$SCRATCH/payload.json" <<JSON; ...'. Cross-references MP-COMMANDS.md mp-scratch surface; flags the /tmp anti-pattern.

acceptance_criteria.description: Closure: `cargo test -p mp && mp validate --summary` exits 0.
acceptance_criteria.evidence: AC-04 (closure) verified: cargo test -p mp && mp validate --summary exits 0. Pre-close-out validate was 14 G6 errors + 1 W44; post-close-out is 0 errors / 0 warnings. Scope narrowed from cargo test -p mp -p raul (broad, multi-crate) to single-crate per §3.2.1 + L53. M116's affected-crate set is {mp} (S1, S3: plan-zone, master-plan/AGENTS.md; S2: crates/mp/src/cli.rs; S4: closure). No code changes in crates/raul/; verifying only -p mp is correct.

design_decisions.choice: edit-tool batch counter — option (b): document the failure mode + grep verify pattern in master-plan/AGENTS.md. The edit tool is external (pi harness / Cursor / OpenCode tooling) and is not in-tree. Option (a) 'patch the edit tool' is not actionable in this repo. The grep verify pattern: after any batch edit, run grep -c '<expected-new>' <file> to confirm the replacement count matches the batch size. Add a 'Verify batch edits' rule in AGENTS.md with this pattern near the edit guidance.
design_decisions.rationale: The edit-tool batch success counter reporting matches-not-found as matches-attempted is a real risk (entry 17 sub-2 dogfood-log). Option (b) gives agents a reliable verification workflow without requiring changes to external tooling. The pattern is actionable immediately and covers the failure mode.

steps.action: Resolve the edit-tool batch success counter reliability gap (entry 17 sub-2). Either (a) patch the edit tool so a batch with non-unique oldText fails fast with a clear error (preferred — silent failure risks shipping bugs), OR (b) document the failure mode in AGENTS.md and add a 'grep verify' pattern: after every batch edit, run grep -c '<expected-new>' <file> to confirm the replacement count matches the batch size. Pick the lower-friction option; document the choice.

steps.action:
Tighten master-plan/AGENTS.md with a dedicated 'Temporary workspace' subsection (or an explicit cross-reference near mp milestone update --json). Add a concrete, copy-pasteable example:

  SCRATCH=$(mp scratch new m-update)
  mp milestone update <id> --json @$SCRATCH/file.json

Note: always run mp scratch new to get a fresh temp path — do not hardcode .mp-scratch paths. The \$SCRATCH variable must be set from the mp scratch output, not from a fixed string. Resolves entry 13 (agents wrote temp JSON to repo root instead of using mp scratch).
